- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- llm-council: Run any question, idea, or decision through a council of 5 AI advisors who independently analyze it, peer-review each other anonymously, and synthesize a final verdict. Based on Karpathy's LLM Council methodology. MANDATORY TRIGGERS: 'council this', 'run the council', 'war room this', 'pressure-test this', 'stress-test this', 'debate this'. STRONG TRIGGERS (use when combined with a real decision or tradeoff): 'should I X or Y', 'which option', 'what would you do', 'is this the right move', 'validate this', 'get multiple perspectives', 'I can't decide', 'I'm torn between'. Do NOT trigger on simple yes/no questions, factual lookups, or casual 'should I' without a meaningful tradeoff (e.g. 'should I use markdown' is not a council question). DO trigger when the user presents a genuine decision with stakes, multiple options, and context that suggests they want it pressure-tested from multiple angles.
- act-review: Assess inline code review comments and apply the valid ones via a fresh subagent
- build-skill: Draft and write a new Claude Code skill based on a recurring task pattern
- doc-sync: Inspect recent changes and draft any missing README section or update
- finalise: Run the project's mandatory finalisation checklist before reporting any task as done
- test-sync: Bring test coverage (mocks, unit tests, Storybook, Playwright) up to date with uncommitted changes
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Issue type for a user story.","iconUrl":"https://toastboy.atlassian.net/images/icons/issuetypes/story.svg","name":"Story","subtask":false,"hierarchyLevel":0},"components":[],"created":"2026-07-31T15:08:12.196+0100","description":"Follow-on from the SYS-584/586 Container/Paper audit. That work fixed pages that double-wrapped a component's own sizing, but left several pages alone as "legitimate page-authored content". A full repo grep (`grep -rl "from '@mantine'" src/app --include="page.tsx"`) shows the real scope is much larger: **23 page.tsx files** import directly from Mantine, not 5.

**Goal:** generalise the rule fully — a `page.tsx` should only fetch data, wire up server actions, and compose components; it should never itself import from `@mantine/core` or any other Mantine package.

**Scope, grouped by pattern:**

1. **Static page-authored content → own component.** No reusable data component to fold sizing into; the page IS the content. Extract each into a dedicated component: `rules`, `familytree` (Flex/Title/Text wrapper around the existing `FamilyTree` component), `tables`, `countrymap`, `info`, `footy/page.tsx` (home page hero), `docs/admin`, `docs/migration` (small shared wrapper for the two MDX pages).
2. **Single-component wrap with no sizing of its own** — same gap as `NewGameForm` had before this audit. `turnout/page.tsx` wraps `Turnout` in `Stack w="100%" p="xl" align="center"`; fold that into `Turnout` itself, page becomes a Fragment.
3. **Repeated "year page shell" pattern** — `winners`, `books`, `curse`, `games`, and `table/[table]` all duplicate the same `Group justify="center"><TitleWithYearDropdown .../></Group>` (plus an outer `Stack`/`Flex`) around one data component. This is a strong candidate for a single shared component (e.g. a `YearPageHeading` or similar) rather than five near-identical copies of the same Mantine layout.
4. **Repeated error/status notification pattern** — `auth/accountdeleted`, `auth/reset-password` (missing-token branch), `auth/claim/[token]` (invalid-invitation branch), `downloadmydata` (two branches), `profile` (two branches), and `admin/users` (fetch-error branch) all render a `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red"/"blue">{message}</Notification>` (or, for `response/page.tsx`, a `Box`+`Text`+`Anchor` variant) directly in the page. Extract a single shared component (e.g. `StatusNotification`) covering both shapes rather than duplicating the pattern seven times.
5. **Genuine multi-component composition needing its own wrapper** — `admin/page.tsx` (dashboard: two independent admin widgets in a `Flex`) and `game/[id]/page.tsx` (`GameDaySummary` + conditional `GameResultForm` in a `Flex`) each arrange more than one component together. This is legitimate page-level composition (per the SYS-586 council verdict), but it still means the page imports Mantine directly — give each its own dedicated wrapper component so the page itself stays Mantine-free.

**Also still in scope from the original ticket:**

* Extend the existing ESLint override at `eslint.config.mjs` (`files: ["src/app/**/page.{ts,tsx}"]`, which already bans the `'use client'` directive in pages via `no-restricted-syntax`) with a `no-restricted-imports` rule banning `@mantine/*` imports in page files, so the rule is enforced mechanically rather than by convention/review.

**Acceptance criteria:**

* No `page.tsx` in `src/app/**` imports from any `@mantine/*` package; enforced by an ESLint rule, not just documented.
* Every page above renders via a dedicated component (new or extended), each with its own test coverage matching the codebase's component-test conventions: accessible selectors, real Mantine rendering, no reliance on Mantine internals.
* `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all clean.

aiTitle: Evaluate page route component composition strategy

content.text:
Looked at SYS-600 and the current ESLint config — worth noting the ban isn't live yet (only the `'use client'` restriction is enforced today in the pages override); the `no-restricted-imports` rule for `@mantine/*` in pages is what this ticket proposes adding.

My take: keep the blanket ban. The RSC dot-notation bug itself doesn't require it (that only bites property access on a `'use client'` export, so a page importing `Flex` directly and composing two components inside it wouldn't trigger it) — but the real value is that "pages only fetch, wire actions, and compose" becomes mechanically enforceable rather than a per-PR judgment call, which matches how this codebase already handles the client/server split (categorical rule over case-by-case exception, per the `require-use-client` rationale in CLAUDE.md). The cost is genuinely minor boilerplate for case 5 in the ticket (`admin/page.tsx`, `game/[id]/page.tsx`) — a one-line `Flex` wrapping two components now needs its own wrapper file and test, even though nothing there is reusable or complex enough to *need* isolation on its own merits.

Want me to start on the extraction work, or do you want to revisit the ticket's scope first?

- Failure branch: `<Stack>` wrapping `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red" withCloseButton={false}>{errorMessage}</Notification>` **plus** `<Anchor href="/footy">Return to the home page</Anchor>` as a sibling.
- Success branch: `redirect('/footy/profile')` (no JSX rendered at all on success).
- Notification is NOT the only content here — always paired with an `Anchor` inside a `Stack`.

**5. `src/app/footy/auth/verify/enquiry/[token]/page.tsx`**
- Calls `deliverContactEnquiry(token)`; catches, `errorMessage = toPublicMessage(error, 'Unable to deliver your message.')`.
- Failure branch: `<Stack>` + `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red" withCloseButton={false}>{errorMessage}</Notification>` + `<Anchor href="/footy">Return to the home page</Anchor>`.
- Success branch (no errorMessage): `<Stack>` + `<Notification icon={<IconCheck/>} color="teal" withCloseButton={false}>Thanks for your message. We will get back to you soon.</Notification>` + `<Anchor href="/footy">Return to the home page</Anchor>`.
- This is the only file with BOTH a success notification (green/teal + check icon) and a failure notification, each paired with the same anchor. Confirms the pattern needs a `color`/`icon` that varies for success vs failure, plus a literal message string for success and dynamic string for failure.

**6. `src/app/footy/auth/verify/extra-email/[token]/page.tsx`**
- Calls `verifyEmail(token)`; catches, `errorMessage = toPublicMessage(error, 'Unable to verify email.')`.
- Failure branch: `<Stack>` + `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red" withCloseButton={false}>{errorMessage}</Notification>` + `<Anchor href="/footy/profile">Return to your profile</Anchor>` (different href/label than #4/#5 — "Return to your profile").
- Success branch: `redirect('/footy/profile')`, no JSX.

**7. `src/app/footy/(authenticated)/downloadmydata/page.tsx`**
- Two independent failure branches, both plain `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red">` (no `withCloseButton` prop set — defaults true, unlike files 3/4/5/6 which explicitly set `false`):
  - No `playerId` (from `getCurrentUser()`): children = literal JSX text `This account is not linked to a player profile yet.` (no `<Text>` wrapper, no variable).
  - `!player` after fetching: children = literal `Failed to load player data.`
- No anchor in either branch; each Notification is the sole content.
- Success branch: builds a `payload` object and renders `<DownloadMyData data={serialisedPayload} />` — not a notification, substantial data-fetch/transform logic (5 parallel service calls + totals computation).

**8. `src/app/footy/(authenticated)/profile/page.tsx`**
- Structurally identical pattern to #7: two failure branches with plain `<Notification icon={<IconX/>} color="red">` (no `withCloseButton`), literal text children (`This account is not linked to a player profile yet.` and `Failed to load player profile.`), no anchor, sole content each.
- Success branch: renders `<><AutoRefresh channels={FootyChannel.Players} /><PlayerProfileForm .../></>` — not a notification.

**9. `src/app/footy/admin/users/page.tsx`**
- Different variant: uses `<Text c="red">{toPublicMessage(error, 'Failed to fetch users.')}</Text>` directly — NOT a `Notification` component at all, no icon, no color prop on a Notification (just Mantine `Text` color prop). This is the "Box+Text" style variant referenced in the prompt (though it's bare `Text`, no `Box`/`Anchor`).
- Triggered inside a try/catch around `listUsersAction()`.
- Success branch: `<><AutoRefresh channels={FootyChannel.Users} /><AdminUserList users={users} setAdminRole={setAdminRoleAction} /></>`.
- Structural outlier: no icon, no `Notification` wrapper — just colored text.

**10. `src/app/footy/response/[token]/page.tsx`**
- Another outlier: no `Notification` at all. Uses `<Text>Invitation details are missing.</Text>` + `<Anchor href="/footy/game">Go to the game page</Anchor>` inside a fragment `<>...</>` when `getGameInvitationResponseDetails(token)` returns falsy. No icon, no color prop anywhere.
- Success branch: renders `<GameInvitationResponseForm details={details} onSubmitGameInvitationResponse={submitGameInvitationResponse} />`.

### Assessment: can one `StatusNotification` component cover all 10?

Not cleanly with a single trivial `{message, color, icon, variant, anchor}` API — there are real structural differences to account for:

- **Two distinct rendering families**: `Notification`-based (files 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 — 8 of 10) vs plain `Text`(+`Anchor`)-based with no icon/notification chrome at all (files 9 and 10). A shared component would need a `variant: 'notification' | 'text'` prop (matching the "Box+Text+Anchor variant" the prompt anticipated) to cover 9 and 10, or those two could reasonably be left out of the shared component (they're not really the same visual pattern — no icon, no colored notification box).
- **`withCloseButton`**: explicitly `false` in files 3,4,5,6; left at default (`true`) in files 1,2,7,8. Needs to be a prop (default true, override false) — not a hardcoded constant.
- **Anchor is optional and varies**: absent in 1,2,3,7,8,9(has one)/10(has one); present in 4,5,6 (all `red`/error) each with different `href`/label (`/footy` "Return to the home page" ×2, `/footy/profile` "Return to your profile"); present in 9/10 style too. So `anchor?: { href: string; label: string }` fits well for the `Notification`-family files that have one (4, 5, 6) plus the two `Text` outliers (9 doesn't have an anchor, 10 does).
- **Message content type varies**: literal hardcoded JSX text (1, 7, 8) vs dynamic string variables from `toPublicMessage()` (3, 4, 5 error branch, 6, 9). A `message: React.ReactNode` prop handles both.
- **Color/icon pairing varies**: `red`+`IconX` (2,3,4,5 err,6,7,8), `blue`+`IconX` (1 — non-error info), `teal`+`IconCheck` (5 success). So `color` and `icon` must be independent props, not derived from a single `severity` enum, unless you add a `'blue'` info variant.
- **Wrapping context differs**: standalone (1,2,3,7,8) vs wrapped in `<Stack>` with a sibling `<Anchor>` (4,5,6) — but this is just consumption-side layout, easily handled by having the shared component itself optionally render the anchor internally (via the `anchor` prop) rather than requiring callers to wrap in `Stack`.
- **File 5 is the only site needing two calls of the component** (error state and success state) in the same page — not a structural blocker, just confirms the component must support both colors/icons via props rather than being error-only.
- **Files 9 and 10 have no icon/Notification chrome at all** — forcing them into a `Notification`-styled shared component would change their visual appearance unless the component supports a `variant='plain'` (bare colored `Text` + optional `Anchor`, no `Notification` box) as literally the "Box+Text+Anchor" variant mentioned in your prompt.

**Conclusion**: A `StatusNotification` component with props like `{ variant: 'notification' | 'plain', message: ReactNode, color: MantineColor, icon?: ReactNode, withCloseButton?: boolean, anchor?: { href: string; label: string } }` would cover all 10 call sites structurally, but note it's genuinely two different visual variants (8 Notification-box sites + 2 plain-Text sites), and files 7/8 have identical dual-branch logic that could even share a slightly higher-level "PlayerNotLinked" pattern on top of the base component. No site has additional non-trivial JSX inside the notification itself beyond text/variable content, so the "message" prop as `ReactNode` is sufficient everywhere.</result>

content.text:
All three Explore agents have reported back. Plan mode was exited automatically during the reconnect, but since you'd asked me to *plan* (not yet implement), here's the consolidated plan rather than a launched implementation.

## SYS-600 implementation plan

**Mechanical enforcement first:** extend the existing `eslint.config.mjs` override for `files: ['src/app/**/page.{ts,tsx}']` with a `no-restricted-imports` rule banning `@mantine/*` — same block that already bans `'use client'` there. Do this last in practice (once all 23 pages are clean) so CI doesn't fail mid-refactor, but it's the acceptance criterion that pins the whole thing down.

### Group 1 — static content → own component (6 pages, 6 new components)
Each page keeps only its data fetch / `metadata` export; all Mantine JSX moves into a new `'use client'` component in `src/components/`:

| Page | New component | Props |
|---|---|---|
| `rules/page.tsx` | `RulesContent` | none (pure static) |
| `familytree/page.tsx` | wrapper around existing `FamilyTree` (e.g. `FamilyTreeIntro`) | `data: FamilyTreeNodeType` |
| `tables/page.tsx` | `TablesIntro` | none (wraps `TableIndexList`) |
| `countrymap/page.tsx` | `CountryMapIntro` | `countries`, plus the derived count (or derive client-side from `countries`) |
| `info/page.tsx` | `InfoContent` | `onSendEnquiry` (passes through to `EnquiryForm`) |
| `footy/page.tsx` (home) | `HomeContent` | `year`, `tables`, `tableRecords` — the `notFound()` check on `year` stays server-side in the page |

### Group 2 — fold into existing component (1 page, 0 new components)
`turnout/page.tsx`: move the `Stack p="xl" align="center"` wrapper into `Turnout.tsx` itself (around its existing `Paper`). `AutoRefresh` stays as a page-level sibling (matches the `game/[id]` model), so the page becomes:
```tsx
return (
  <>
    <AutoRefresh channels={[FootyChannel.Games, FootyChannel.Results]} />
    <Turnout turnout={turnout} />
  </>
);
```

### Group 3 — year page shell (5 pages, 1 new shared component + 1 existing edit)
New `YearPageShell` component absorbing the outer `Stack`/`Flex` + `Group`+`TitleWithYearDropdown` (+ optional `subheading`, + optional `autoRefreshChannels`), taking `children` for the per-page data component:
```tsx
<YearPageShell title="Winners: " year={year} validYears={allYears} autoRefreshChannels={FootyChannel.Results}>
  <WinnersTable ... />
</YearPageShell>
```
Applies cleanly to `books`, `curse`, `games` (via `subheading`), and `table/[table]`. **One wrinkle:** `winners/page.tsx` currently has an extra `Flex` mapping multiple `WinnersTable` instances inside the shell — that Flex is Mantine and page-specific, so it needs folding into `WinnersTable` itself (accept the full per-table records array and do its own internal wrap-Flex) rather than living in the page.

### Group 4 — status notification (10 pages, 1 new shared component)
New `StatusNotification` component covering both shapes found:
```tsx
interface Props {
  variant?: 'notification' | 'plain'; // plain = bare Text, no icon/box (admin/users, response/[token])
  message: ReactNode;
  color: MantineColor;
  icon?: ReactNode;
  withCloseButton?: boolean;
  anchor?: { href: string; label: string };
}
```
Covers: `accountdeleted`, `reset-password`, `auth/claim/[token]`, `auth/claim/[token]/finish`, `verify/enquiry/[token]` (both branches), `verify/extra-email/[token]`, `downloadmydata` (×2 branches), `profile` (×2 branches), `admin/users`, `response/[token]`.

### Group 5 — dedicated wrapper for composition (1 page, 1 new component)
New `AdminDashboard` component absorbing `Container`/`Center`/`Title`/`Flex` around the two existing widgets:
```tsx
return (
  <AdminDashboard
    onUpdatePlayerRecords={updatePlayerRecords}
    getProgress={getProgress}
    onExportAuth={authExport}
  />
);
```
Mirrors the already-shipped `game/[id]/page.tsx` + `GameDaySummary` pattern exactly.

### Coverage
Every new component gets a `*.vitest.spec.tsx` next to it (accessible selectors, real Mantine rendering per CLAUDE.md conventions) to keep the ≥90% coverage bar; `Turnout` and `WinnersTable`'s existing specs get updated for their new responsibilities. Stories only where the existing sibling pattern already has them (e.g. `FamilyTree` has `.stories.tsx`).

### Totals
23 pages changed · 9 new components (`RulesContent`, `FamilyTreeIntro`, `TablesIntro`, `CountryMapIntro`, `InfoContent`, `HomeContent`, `YearPageShell`, `StatusNotification`, `AdminDashboard`) · 2 existing components edited (`Turnout`, `WinnersTable`) · 1 ESLint rule addition.

import { Flex, Text, Title } from '@mantine/core';

export const metadata = { title: 'Rules' };

const RulesPage = () => {
    return (
        <>
            <Flex
                gap="md"
                align="flex-start"
                direction="column"
                p="xl"
            >
                <Title order={1}>Toastboy FC: Rules</Title>

                <Text>
                    Broadly speaking, we want a fast, competitive game with as
                    small a risk of injury as possible. There's no referee:
                    we call our own mistakes like the gentlemen we are.
                </Text>

                <Text>
                    Violent conduct is of course not allowed, and results in a
                    direct free kick. For safety reasons, sliding tackles and
                    heading the ball are also banned. Pushing and barging are
                    not allowed: this isn't a non-contact sport, but we do
                    want to avoid players being bundled into the wall/floor and
                    breaking something.
                </Text>

                <Text>
                    The ball is not allowed over head height - infringements
                    result in an indirect free kick. The only exception is if
                    the ball goes high off the goalkeeper: if it was a
                    deflection, we play on. If it was deliberate, the goalie
                    gets the ball back. Meint doesn't like this rule, and I
                    can see his point :-> Practicality dictates that we use
                    the blue line around 3 of the 4 walls in the hall as the
                    “official” head height, although if the ball
                    hits the nets between the two halves of the hall we have to
                    call that over head height too.
                </Text>

                <Text>
                    The goalie can't deliberately leave their area (the red
                    ‘D’), and no other player can enter it. If a
                    player's momentum takes them slightly the wrong side of
                    the line, it will be overlooked.
                </Text>

                <Text>
                    For all free kicks, defenders must be at least 2 meters away
                    from the ball, or as far as possible if the ball is near the
                    goalie's area.
                </Text>

                <Text>
                    Substitutions and goalie changes can happen at any time. By
                    convention, play stops whenever a player has to tie his
                    laces or return the ball to the clodhopping oafs next door
                    who are always hoofing their ball into our half. On hot days
                    we have a quick break half way through the game for drinks.
                </Text>

                <Text>
                    After every game, we retire to a local pub for a few jars.
                    Cheers!
                </Text>
            </Flex>
        </>
    );
};

export default RulesPage;

import { Anchor, Container, Flex, Text, Title } from '@mantine/core';

import { sendEnquiry } from '@/actions/sendEnquiry';
import { EnquiryForm } from '@/components/EnquiryForm/EnquiryForm';

export const metadata = { title: 'Info' };

const Page = () => {
    return (
        <>
            <Flex
                gap="md"
                align="flex-start"
                direction="column"
                p="xl"
            >
                <Title order={1}>Toastboy FC: Tuesday Night Football</Title>
                <Text>
                    We play a friendly five-a-side footy game amongst ourselves
                    every Tuesday night between 6 and 7pm at the{' '}
                    <Anchor href="http://www.kelseykerridge.co.uk/">
                        Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre
                    </Anchor>{' '}
                    in Cambridge (for our international visitors, that's
                    "soccer", "center" and "Cambridge, England").
                </Text>
                <Container fluid>
                    <iframe
                        src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d2445.3263160975907!2d0.1279577126825085!3d52.20111725967227!2m3!1f0!2f0!3f0!3m2!1i1024!2i768!4f13.1!3m3!1m2!1s0x47d8709a9a53b7ff%3A0x34e196dca006ac25!2sKelsey%20Kerridge%20Sports%20Centre!5e0!3m2!1sen!2suk!4v1716736866954!5m2!1sen!2suk"
                        width="100%"
                        height="450"
                        allowFullScreen={true}
                        title="Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre"
                        referrerPolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
                    />
                </Container>
                <Text>
                    <Anchor href="/footy/rules">
                        Here's an outline of the rules of our games.
                    </Anchor>{' '}
                    The standard of play's not too high, although we're not
                    complete duffers - but we do play to win. After all, there's
                    the glory of the trophies which are presented at the
                    sumptuous end-of-year awards ceremonies at stake. Here's how
                    it works. Every player who's on the winning team each week
                    gets 3 points, or 1 for a draw. There are 3 trophies up for
                    grabs:
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    <Anchor href="/footy/points">Points</Anchor>. Simple -
                    whoever has the biggest points total at the end of the year
                    wins the Pewterware.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    <Anchor href="/footy/averages">Averages</Anchor>. Just the
                    points total divided by the number of games played, but note
                    you have to have played a minimum of 5 games in a year to
                    qualify.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    <Anchor href="/footy/stalwart">Stalwart</Anchor>. To
                    encourage people to play regularly. The winner is the one
                    who's played the most games in a year.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    Each week an automated email goes out, inviting players to
                    log in to the site and say whether or not they can play.
                    Once we have enough players, we run the picker script which
                    picks the fairest possible teams based on the age and number
                    of wins in the last 10 games played of each player. I ask
                    for four pounds fifty from each player to cover the cost of
                    the hall booking and things like footballs and bibs. We
                    nearly always go for a pint after the game: everyone is
                    welcome. We usually go to the Grain and Hop Store and then
                    often for a bite to eat.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    There's an extra little bonus something at the award
                    ceremony for the person who has the best average response
                    time throughout the year: keep track of where you stand in
                    the <Anchor href="/footy/speedy">Captain Speedy</Anchor>{' '}
                    table.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    We're always looking for players, so if you want to join the
                    list, fill in the form below!
                </Text>
                <EnquiryForm onSendEnquiry={sendEnquiry} />
            </Flex>
        </>
    );
};

export default Page;

'use client';

import { Flex, Text, Title } from '@mantine/core';

export const RulesContent = () => {
    return (
        <Flex
            gap="md"
            align="flex-start"
            direction="column"
            p="xl"
        >
            <Title order={1}>Toastboy FC: Rules</Title>

            <Text>
                Broadly speaking, we want a fast, competitive game with as
                small a risk of injury as possible. There's no referee:
                we call our own mistakes like the gentlemen we are.
            </Text>

            <Text>
                Violent conduct is of course not allowed, and results in a
                direct free kick. For safety reasons, sliding tackles and
                heading the ball are also banned. Pushing and barging are not
                allowed: this isn't a non-contact sport, but we do want
                to avoid players being bundled into the wall/floor and
                breaking something.
            </Text>

            <Text>
                The ball is not allowed over head height - infringements
                result in an indirect free kick. The only exception is if the
                ball goes high off the goalkeeper: if it was a deflection, we
                play on. If it was deliberate, the goalie gets the ball back.
                Meint doesn't like this rule, and I can see his point :->
                Practicality dictates that we use the blue line around 3 of
                the 4 walls in the hall as the “official” head
                height, although if the ball hits the nets between the two
                halves of the hall we have to call that over head height too.
            </Text>

            <Text>
                The goalie can't deliberately leave their area (the red
                ‘D’), and no other player can enter it. If a
                player's momentum takes them slightly the wrong side of
                the line, it will be overlooked.
            </Text>

            <Text>
                For all free kicks, defenders must be at least 2 meters away
                from the ball, or as far as possible if the ball is near the
                goalie's area.
            </Text>

            <Text>
                Substitutions and goalie changes can happen at any time. By
                convention, play stops whenever a player has to tie his laces
                or return the ball to the clodhopping oafs next door who are
                always hoofing their ball into our half. On hot days we have
                a quick break half way through the game for drinks.
            </Text>

            <Text>
                After every game, we retire to a local pub for a few jars.
                Cheers!
            </Text>
        </Flex>
    );
};

import { EnquiryForm } from '@/components/EnquiryForm/EnquiryForm';

export interface Props {
    onSendEnquiry: SendEnquiryProxy;

    return (
        <Flex
            gap="md"
            align="flex-start"
            direction="column"
            p="xl"
        >
            <Title order={1}>Toastboy FC: Tuesday Night Football</Title>
            <Text>
                We play a friendly five-a-side footy game amongst ourselves
                every Tuesday night between 6 and 7pm at the{' '}
                <Anchor href="http://www.kelseykerridge.co.uk/">
                    Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre
                </Anchor>{' '}
                in Cambridge (for our international visitors, that's
                "soccer", "center" and "Cambridge, England").
            </Text>
            <Container fluid>
                <iframe
                    src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d2445.3263160975907!2d0.1279577126825085!3d52.20111725967227!2m3!1f0!2f0!3f0!3m2!1i1024!2i768!4f13.1!3m3!1m2!1s0x47d8709a9a53b7ff%3A0x34e196dca006ac25!2sKelsey%20Kerridge%20Sports%20Centre!5e0!3m2!1sen!2suk!4v1716736866954!5m2!1sen!2suk"
                    width="100%"
                    height="450"
                    allowFullScreen={true}
                    title="Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre"
                    referrerPolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
                />
            </Container>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/rules">
                    Here's an outline of the rules of our games.
                </Anchor>{' '}
                The standard of play's not too high, although we're not
                complete duffers - but we do play to win. After all, there's
                the glory of the trophies which are presented at the
                sumptuous end-of-year awards ceremonies at stake. Here's how
                it works. Every player who's on the winning team each week
                gets 3 points, or 1 for a draw. There are 3 trophies up for
                grabs:
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/points">Points</Anchor>. Simple -
                whoever has the biggest points total at the end of the year
                wins the Pewterware.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/averages">Averages</Anchor>. Just the
                points total divided by the number of games played, but note
                you have to have played a minimum of 5 games in a year to
                qualify.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/stalwart">Stalwart</Anchor>. To
                encourage people to play regularly. The winner is the one
                who's played the most games in a year.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                Each week an automated email goes out, inviting players to
                log in to the site and say whether or not they can play. Once
                we have enough players, we run the picker script which picks
                the fairest possible teams based on the age and number of
                wins in the last 10 games played of each player. I ask for
                four pounds fifty from each player to cover the cost of the
                hall booking and things like footballs and bibs. We nearly
                always go for a pint after the game: everyone is welcome. We
                usually go to the Grain and Hop Store and then often for a
                bite to eat.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                There's an extra little bonus something at the award ceremony
                for the person who has the best average response time
                throughout the year: keep track of where you stand in the{' '}
                <Anchor href="/footy/speedy">Captain Speedy</Anchor> table.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                We're always looking for players, so if you want to join the
                list, fill in the form below!
            </Text>
            <EnquiryForm onSendEnquiry={onSendEnquiry} />
        </Flex>
    );
};

import { Anchor, Container, Flex, Text, Title } from '@mantine/core';

import { sendEnquiry } from '@/actions/sendEnquiry';
import { EnquiryForm } from '@/components/EnquiryForm/EnquiryForm';

export const metadata = { title: 'Info' };

const Page = () => {
    return (
        <>
            <Flex
                gap="md"
                align="flex-start"
                direction="column"
                p="xl"
            >
                <Title order={1}>Toastboy FC: Tuesday Night Football</Title>
                <Text>
                    We play a friendly five-a-side footy game amongst ourselves
                    every Tuesday night between 6 and 7pm at the{' '}
                    <Anchor href="http://www.kelseykerridge.co.uk/">
                        Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre
                    </Anchor>{' '}
                    in Cambridge (for our international visitors, that's
                    "soccer", "center" and "Cambridge, England").
                </Text>
                <Container fluid>
                    <iframe
                        src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d2445.3263160975907!2d0.1279577126825085!3d52.20111725967227!2m3!1f0!2f0!3f0!3m2!1i1024!2i768!4f13.1!3m3!1m2!1s0x47d8709a9a53b7ff%3A0x34e196dca006ac25!2sKelsey%20Kerridge%20Sports%20Centre!5e0!3m2!1sen!2suk!4v1716736866954!5m2!1sen!2suk"
                        width="100%"
                        height="450"
                        allowFullScreen={true}
                        title="Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre"
                        referrerPolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
                    />
                </Container>
                <Text>
                    <Anchor href="/footy/rules">
                        Here's an outline of the rules of our games.
                    </Anchor>{' '}
                    The standard of play's not too high, although we're not
                    complete duffers - but we do play to win. After all, there's
                    the glory of the trophies which are presented at the
                    sumptuous end-of-year awards ceremonies at stake. Here's how
                    it works. Every player who's on the winning team each week
                    gets 3 points, or 1 for a draw. There are 3 trophies up for
                    grabs:
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    <Anchor href="/footy/points">Points</Anchor>. Simple -
                    whoever has the biggest points total at the end of the year
                    wins the Pewterware.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    <Anchor href="/footy/averages">Averages</Anchor>. Just the
                    points total divided by the number of games played, but note
                    you have to have played a minimum of 5 games in a year to
                    qualify.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    <Anchor href="/footy/stalwart">Stalwart</Anchor>. To
                    encourage people to play regularly. The winner is the one
                    who's played the most games in a year.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    Each week an automated email goes out, inviting players to
                    log in to the site and say whether or not they can play.
                    Once we have enough players, we run the picker script which
                    picks the fairest possible teams based on the age and number
                    of wins in the last 10 games played of each player. I ask
                    for four pounds fifty from each player to cover the cost of
                    the hall booking and things like footballs and bibs. We
                    nearly always go for a pint after the game: everyone is
                    welcome. We usually go to the Grain and Hop Store and then
                    often for a bite to eat.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    There's an extra little bonus something at the award
                    ceremony for the person who has the best average response
                    time throughout the year: keep track of where you stand in
                    the <Anchor href="/footy/speedy">Captain Speedy</Anchor>{' '}
                    table.
                </Text>
                <Text>
                    We're always looking for players, so if you want to join the
                    list, fill in the form below!
                </Text>
                <EnquiryForm onSendEnquiry={sendEnquiry} />
            </Flex>
        </>
    );
};

export default Page;

content.text:
All 23 pages, the ESLint rule, and 10 new components (including `WinnersGrid`, a small addition beyond the original plan to extract winners' per-table grid layout) are in place, with full test coverage. Final verification summary:

- **`npm run typecheck`** — clean
- **`npm run lint`** — clean
- **`npm run format:check`** — clean
- **`npx knip`** — clean, no unused files/exports
- **`npm run test`** (full suite: actions, api, components, pages, services, lib) — 238 files, 1978 tests passed (1 pre-existing skip, 4 pre-existing todos)
- **Components layer coverage** — 100% statements/branches/functions/lines
- **Pages layer coverage** — 97.3% statements (uncovered lines are pre-existing, in files I didn't touch)

One deviation from the plan worth flagging: `winners/page.tsx` needed an extra `WinnersGrid` component (not in the original 9) to absorb the `Flex`-wrapped map over multiple `WinnersTable` instances — that JSX couldn't fold into `YearPageShell` (it's winners-specific) or `WinnersTable` (which renders one table, not a grid) cleanly, so it got its own small wrapper. That brings the total to **10 new components** instead of 9.

I didn't run `npm run build` (it requires `op run --env-file ./.env --` for secrets you'd need to authorize) — the finalisation checklist's required steps (typecheck/lint/format/knip) plus the full test suite all pass, so I'd suggest running the build yourself when convenient to get the last word before deploying.

input.summary: Silence Vite "configLoader: native" ESM-in-CommonJS warning on vitest config files
input.description:
Every `npm run test*` invocation prints one warning per vitest config file loaded, e.g.:

```
(!) Your Vite config uses features that are unsupported by `configLoader: 'native'`, which is planned to become the default in a future major version of Vite:
  - ESM syntax in a file loaded as CommonJS (vitest.unit.config.ts:1:1). Use a `.mjs` extension or set `"type": "module"` in the closest package.json
Set `VITE_CONFIG_NATIVE_IGNORE_WARNING=true` to suppress this warning.
```

**Cause:** `package.json` has no `"type": "module"` field, so it defaults to CommonJS. All of the repo's `vitest.*.config.ts` files use ESM `import` syntax (e.g. `import path from 'node:path';`), which Vite's upcoming default `configLoader: 'native'` doesn't support for CJS-mode `.ts` files.

**Affected files** (all currently loaded by at least one `npm run test*` script):
- `vitest.config.ts`
- `vitest.unit.config.ts`
- `vitest.actions.config.ts`
- `vitest.api.config.ts`
- `vitest.components.config.ts`
- `vitest.pages.config.ts`
- `vitest.lib.config.ts`
- `vitest.services.config.ts`
- `vitest.picker.integration.config.ts`

**Suggested fix:** rename each `vitest.*.config.ts` to `vitest.*.config.mts` (the narrower fix Vite itself suggests) rather than adding `"type": "module"` to `package.json`, since the latter is repo-wide and could affect unrelated CommonJS-assuming tooling. This requires updating:
1. The `--config vitest.*.config.ts` flag in every matching script in `package.json` (`test`, `test:watch`, `test:coverage`, `test:actions[:coverage]`, `test:api[:coverage]`, `test:components[:coverage]`, `test:pages[:coverage]`, `test:lib[:coverage]`, `test:services[:coverage]`, `test:picker:integration`).
2. The `projects: [...]` array of sibling config filenames inside `vitest.unit.config.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Running any `npm run test*` script produces no `configLoader: 'native'` / ESM-in-CommonJS warning.
- All test suites still pass with the renamed config files (`npm run test`, `npm run test:pages`, `npm run test:components`, etc.).
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, and `npx knip` remain clean.

content.text:
All checks are in. Summary:

- **Mocks**: added `__mocks__/ComponentName.tsx` for all 10 new components (`RulesContent`, `FamilyTreeIntro`, `TablesIntro`, `CountryMapIntro`, `InfoContent`, `HomeContent`, `YearPageShell`, `WinnersGrid`, `StatusNotification`, `AdminDashboard`), matching the codebase's established auto-mock pattern.
- **Storybook stories**: added `ComponentName.stories.tsx` for all 10, filed under sensible titles (`Pages/*`, `Tables/WinnersGrid`, `Utilities/StatusNotification`, `Admin/AdminDashboard`). Found and fixed one real bug along the way: `AdminDashboard`'s story initially failed because `AdminUpdatePlayerRecords` polls `getProgress()` on mount, and Storybook's vitest addon resets `fn()` mocks between story runs — a `.mockResolvedValue` set at module scope gets wiped before render. input.summary: Fix duplicate React keys from defaultPlayerRecordDataList mock fixture
input.description:
Any Storybook story or test that renders multiple rows from `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` (`src/tests/mocks/data/playerRecordData.ts`) triggers a React console error:

```
Encountered two children with the same key, `1`. Keys should be unique so that components maintain their identity across updates. Non-unique keys may cause children to be duplicated and/or omitted — the behavior is unsupported and could change in a future version.
```

**Root cause:** `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` is generated as:

```ts
export const defaultPlayerRecordDataList: PlayerRecordDataType[] = Array.from(
    { length: 20 },
    (_, index) =>
        createMockPlayerRecordData({
            points: 100 - 3 * index,
        }),
);
```

`createMockPlayerRecordData` only overrides `points`; every other field — including `id: 1` and `player: defaultPlayer` — comes from `defaultPlayerRecordData`/`defaultPlayerRecord` (`src/tests/mocks/data/playerRecord.ts`) unchanged. So all 20 generated records share the same `id` and the same `player`. Components that key rows by `record.id` (`WinnersTable`, and by extension anything reusing this fixture, e.g. `RecordsTable`, `YearTable`, and the new `HomeContent`/`WinnersGrid` from SYS-600) collide on that key.

Note `playerRecord.ts` already has a properly-varied 100-record fixture, `defaultPlayerRecordList` (unique `id`, varied `playerId`/`year`/stats per entry) — `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` just doesn't follow the same pattern when it wraps those records with `player` data for `PlayerRecordDataType` consumers.

**Suggested fix:** vary `id` (and ideally `playerId`/`player`) per generated entry in `defaultPlayerRecordDataList`, matching the existing pattern in `defaultPlayerRecordList`, so each of the 20 records is genuinely distinct rather than differing only in `points`.

**Affected consumers (currently emit the warning today):**
- `src/components/RecordsTable/RecordsTable.stories.tsx`
- `src/components/WinnersTable/WinnersTable.stories.tsx`
- `src/components/YearTable/YearTable.stories.tsx` (uses a related fixture — verify while fixing)
- `src/components/HomeContent/HomeContent.stories.tsx` (new, from SYS-600 — renders three `RecordsTable`s from this fixture simultaneously, so the warning fires 3x)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` entries have unique `id` values (and ideally non-identical `player`s, to make stories more visually representative).
- No "duplicate key" console error when running `npm run test:storybook` for the affected stories.
- No regressions in existing tests/stories that assert on specific fixture values (e.g. `points: 100 - 3 * index` ordering) — check call sites before changing shape.

content.text:
Created **[SYS-608](https://toastboy.atlassian.net/browse/SYS-608)** — "Fix duplicate React keys from `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` mock fixture."

Root cause confirmed: `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` (`src/tests/mocks/data/playerRecordData.ts`) generates 20 records that only vary `points` — every entry inherits the same `id: 1` and the same `player` from the base fixture, so anything keying rows by `record.id` (`WinnersTable`, `RecordsTable`, `YearTable`, and now `HomeContent`) collides. The ticket points at the fix: `playerRecord.ts` already has a properly-varied 100-record fixture (`defaultPlayerRecordList`) that `defaultPlayerRecordDataList` should follow the same pattern of instead of just cloning `points`.

'use client';

import { Anchor, Container, Flex, Text, Title } from '@mantine/core';

import { EnquiryForm } from '@/components/EnquiryForm/EnquiryForm';
import { SendEnquiryProxy } from '@/types/actions/SendEnquiry';

export interface Props {
    onSendEnquiry: SendEnquiryProxy;
}

export const InfoContent = ({ onSendEnquiry }: Props) => {
    return (
        <Flex
            gap="md"
            align="flex-start"
            direction="column"
            p="xl"
        >
            <Title order={1}>Toastboy FC: Tuesday Night Football</Title>
            <Text>
                We play a friendly five-a-side footy game amongst ourselves
                every Tuesday night between 6 and 7pm at the{' '}
                <Anchor href="https://www.kelseykerridge.co.uk/">
                    Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre
                </Anchor>{' '}
                in Cambridge (for our international visitors, that's "soccer",
                "center" and "Cambridge, England").
            </Text>
            <Container fluid>
                <iframe
                    src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d2445.3263160975907!2d0.1279577126825085!3d52.20111725967227!2m3!1f0!2f0!3f0!3m2!1i1024!2i768!4f13.1!3m3!1m2!1s0x47d8709a9a53b7ff%3A0x34e196dca006ac25!2sKelsey%20Kerridge%20Sports%20Centre!5e0!3m2!1sen!2suk!4v1716736866954!5m2!1sen!2suk"
                    width="100%"
                    height="450"
                    allowFullScreen={true}
                    title="Kelsey Kerridge Sports Centre"
                    referrerPolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
                />
            </Container>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/rules">
                    Here's an outline of the rules of our games.
                </Anchor>{' '}
                The standard of play's not too high, although we're not complete
                duffers - but we do play to win. After all, there's the glory of
                the trophies which are presented at the sumptuous end-of-year
                awards ceremonies at stake. Here's how it works. Every player
                who's on the winning team each week gets 3 points, or 1 for a
                draw. There are 3 trophies up for grabs:
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/points">Points</Anchor>. Simple - whoever
                has the biggest points total at the end of the year wins the
                Pewterware.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/averages">Averages</Anchor>. Just the
                points total divided by the number of games played, but note you
                have to have played a minimum of 5 games in a year to qualify.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                <Anchor href="/footy/stalwart">Stalwart</Anchor>. To encourage
                people to play regularly. The winner is the one who's played the
                most games in a year.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                Each week an automated email goes out, inviting players to log
                in to the site and say whether or not they can play. Once we
                have enough players, we run the picker script which picks the
                fairest possible teams based on the age and number of wins in
                the last 10 games played of each player. I ask for four pounds
                fifty from each player to cover the cost of the hall booking and
                things like footballs and bibs. We nearly always go for a pint
                after the game: everyone is welcome. We usually go to the Grain
                and Hop Store and then often for a bite to eat.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                There's an extra little bonus something at the award ceremony
                for the person who has the best average response time throughout
                the year: keep track of where you stand in the{' '}
                <Anchor href="/footy/speedy">Captain Speedy</Anchor> table.
            </Text>
            <Text>
                We're always looking for players, so if you want to join the
                list, fill in the form below!
            </Text>
            <EnquiryForm onSendEnquiry={onSendEnquiry} />
        </Flex>
    );
};
